questions.question_text: Two masses are separated by distance r. If their separation becomes 2r while the masses stay unchanged, how does their gravitational attraction change?
questions.option_d: It becomes four times as large
questions.explanation: Newton's law gives F ∝ 1/r²; doubling separation divides the force by 2² = 4.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Gravitation, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc109.pdf

questions.question_text: If one mass in a pair is doubled and the separation between them is also doubled, the gravitational force becomes
questions.explanation: The mass factor doubles the force while doubling distance reduces it by four, so the net factor is 2/4 = 1/2.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Gravitation, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc109.pdf

questions.question_text: An astronaut takes the same object from Earth to the Moon. Which statement is correct?
questions.option_a: Its mass stays the same while its weight decreases
questions.option_b: Its mass and weight both become zero
questions.option_c: Its mass decreases but its weight stays unchanged
questions.option_d: Its mass becomes six times larger
questions.explanation: Mass measures inertia and is location-independent; weight is mg and is lower where gravitational acceleration is smaller, including on the Moon.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Gravitation, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc109.pdf

questions.question_text: In a vacuum, a stone and a feather are released from the same height at the same time. Neglecting air resistance, which reaches the ground first?
questions.option_b: The stone, because it has greater mass
questions.option_c: The feather, because it has less inertia
questions.explanation: In free fall near Earth, gravitational acceleration is independent of mass when air resistance is absent.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Gravitation, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc109.pdf

questions.question_text: A skydiver falls faster at first but eventually descends at nearly constant speed. At terminal velocity, which forces are balanced?
questions.option_a: Weight downward and air resistance upward
questions.explanation: At terminal speed the upward drag balances downward weight, so net force and acceleration are approximately zero.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Astronauts in an orbiting spacecraft appear weightless mainly because they
questions.option_a: and the spacecraft are both in continuous free fall around Earth
questions.explanation: Gravity remains significant in orbit; astronauts and spacecraft fall together, so there is little supporting normal force and they feel weightless.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Ignoring Earth's rotation and local geology, how does the value of g generally change as altitude above Earth's surface increases?
questions.option_c: It remains exactly constant at every altitude
questions.explanation: Increasing altitude increases distance from Earth's centre, reducing gravitational acceleration approximately according to an inverse-square relation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Gravitation, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc109.pdf

questions.question_text: For an ideal spherically symmetric Earth, the gravitational field at its exact centre is
questions.explanation: At the centre, pulls from all directions cancel by symmetry; real Earth is not perfectly uniform, but the ideal model gives zero field there.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: For a satellite in a circular orbit, which force provides the required centripetal acceleration?
questions.option_c: A forward magnetic force from Earth
questions.option_d: The satellite's internal force on itself
questions.explanation: Gravity continuously pulls the satellite toward Earth's centre and supplies the centripetal force for its curved orbital path.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person carries a suitcase horizontally at constant height. In the ideal mechanical definition, the upward force on the suitcase does no work during the horizontal motion because
questions.explanation: Work by a force is F·s = Fs cos θ; with force vertical and displacement horizontal, θ = 90° and the work is zero.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc110.pdf

questions.question_text: A box slides across a rough floor and slows down. What is the sign of the work done by kinetic friction on the box?
questions.explanation: Kinetic friction acts opposite the displacement, so its work is negative and the box loses mechanical energy as heat.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc110.pdf

questions.question_text: A constant 50 N force acts along the direction of motion of an object for 4 m. How much work does the force do?
questions.explanation: W = Fs when force and displacement are parallel: 50 × 4 = 200 J.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc110.pdf

questions.question_text: A 10 kg load is lifted vertically by 2 m at constant speed. Taking g = 10 m/s², what work is done against gravity?
questions.explanation: The lifting force balances the 100 N weight; work against gravity is mgh = 10×10×2 = 200 J.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc110.pdf

questions.question_text: A moving object's speed is doubled while its mass remains unchanged. Its kinetic energy becomes
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is ½mv²; doubling speed multiplies it by 2² = 4.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc110.pdf

questions.question_text: Two objects have the same kinetic energy. If object A has four times the mass of object B, what is the ratio of their speeds vA:vB?
questions.explanation: At equal kinetic energy, mv² is constant; quadrupling mass requires speed to halve, so vA:vB = 1:2.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc110.pdf

questions.question_text: The work-energy theorem states that the net work done on an object equals the change in its
questions.explanation: Net work changes an object's kinetic energy: Wnet = ΔK.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from rest from height h and air resistance is negligible. Just before reaching the ground, its lost gravitational potential energy has been converted mainly into
questions.explanation: With negligible losses, conservation of mechanical energy converts gravitational potential energy into kinetic energy during the fall.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc110.pdf

questions.question_text: A pendulum swings between two extreme positions. At the lowest point, its speed and kinetic energy are greatest while its gravitational potential energy is
questions.option_a: least relative to the chosen lowest-point reference
questions.explanation: As the pendulum descends, gravitational potential energy converts to kinetic energy; at the lowest point speed is greatest and potential energy is minimum for that reference.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 60 kg worker climbs a 5 m staircase in 10 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the worker's average power against gravity?
questions.explanation: Work against gravity is mgh = 60×10×5 = 3,000 J; power is work/time = 300 W.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc110.pdf

questions.question_text: One kilowatt-hour is a unit of
questions.explanation: A kilowatt-hour is power multiplied by time, so it measures energy; 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc110.pdf

questions.question_text: A spring is compressed and then released. The energy stored while compressed is primarily
questions.explanation: A deformed elastic spring stores elastic potential energy, which can become kinetic energy when released.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A machine receives 500 J of energy and delivers 350 J of useful output. What is its efficiency?
questions.explanation: Efficiency = useful output/input × 100% = 350/500 × 100% = 70%.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A machine has efficiency less than 100% because some input energy is commonly
questions.option_a: transferred to less useful forms such as heat and sound
questions.option_c: converted into mass in every cycle
questions.option_d: made to violate conservation of energy
questions.explanation: Energy is conserved, but friction and other processes transfer some input into less useful forms, reducing useful output efficiency.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: At a point twice as far from Earth's centre as its surface radius, the gravitational field strength compared with its surface value is approximately
questions.explanation: For a spherical mass outside Earth, g ∝ 1/r²; at 2R it is one-fourth of its value at R.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT physics references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A 2 kg object is raised 5 m above a reference level. Taking g = 10 m/s², its gain in gravitational potential energy is
questions.explanation: Near Earth's surface, ΔU = mgh = 2×10×5 = 100 J.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc110.pdf

questions.question_text: A 1 kg object falls from rest through 20 m near Earth with no air resistance. Taking g = 10 m/s², what speed does it reach just before impact?
questions.explanation: Using v² = 2gh gives v² = 2×10×20 = 400, so v = 20 m/s.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Gravitation and Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc109.pdf

questions.question_text: An object weighs 98 N near Earth's surface where g = 9.8 m/s². What is its mass?
questions.explanation: Weight W = mg; therefore m = 98/9.8 = 10 kg.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Gravitation, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc109.pdf

questions.question_text: A person pushes hard on a rigid wall but the wall does not move. In the mechanical definition of work done on the wall, the work is
questions.option_a: zero because the wall has no displacement
questions.option_b: positive because the force is large
questions.option_c: negative because the wall is heavy
questions.explanation: Mechanical work by a force requires displacement; with zero displacement, the work done on the wall is zero even though the person uses energy internally.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class IX Science, Work and Energy, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/iesc110.pdf
